For ſuch workes exclude grace, are not, & what fauour, and mercie : and chalenge only of debt, and not of gnift. Therfore take heed are the cauſe of here of the Heretkes oo, that vuel exclude Chriſtian mens workes from ſaluatio neceſsity or merit of Saluation, which are done with and by Gods grace, and therfore euidently conſiſt with the ſame, and be ioyned with Gods grace as cauſes of our ſal- uation. God is not Chryſ. ho. 19, inep. Ro. And S. Auguſtine ſaith, not by putting nalice into them, but Authour of ſin- by not imparting his grace vnto them, and that through ther owne deſerts alwaies, and ne. dSix- their owne willes euer properly working the ſame. See Annot. Mat. c. 13,14. Ro. c. 1,21. 10.Becauſe vf increduliy.) He repreſſeth the pride of the Gentils vanting themſelues A paraphraſti- of their receiuing, and of the Iewes reiection, namely in that they thought the Iewes to cal explicati- be forſaken for no other cauſe, but tlat they migh come nto theroomes: decla of the tet, that the direct and proper cauſe of their forſaking, was their incredulity, exhorting concerning the Gentils to beware of the ſame, becauſe they may fal as wel as the other, and that the Iewes and God is as like to execute iuſtice againſt them as againſt the Iewes, as he hath done in Gentils, their many Nations falling to hereſie. ſtāding, falling 28.Accurding to the Ghoſpel.) In reſpect, or, as concerning beleefe in Chriſt and recei- riſing againt, uing the Ghoſpel, they are Gods enemies: by occaſion of whichtheir incredulity, &c. the Gentils found mercie: otherwiſe in reſpect of his ſpecial clection of that Nation, and the promiſes made to the Patriarches, the Iewes are deere to him ſtil. For God neuer promiſeth but he performeth, nor repenteth himſelf of the priuiledges giuen to that Nation. For as you.) As the Gentils which before beleeued not, found mercie and came to faith, when the Iewes did fal: ſo the Iewes not now beleeuing, wben al the Gentile haue obrained mercie, shal in the end of the world by Gods diſpoſition obtaine grace and pardon as the Gentils haue done. Concluded al.) That ſo God taking al Nations and al men in ſinne ( which they fel into, not by his drift or cauſing, but of their owne free wil) may of his mereie cal & con- uert whom and in what order he wil: and the parties haue no cauſe to brag of their de- ſeruings: but both Countries and particular nien may referre their eternal election and their firſt calling and conuerſion, to Chriſt, and to his mercie only: no workes which they had before in their incredulity deſeruing any ſuch thing, though their workes afterward proceeding of faith and grace doe merit Heauen. 33.O depih.) The Apoſtle concludeth that no man ought to ſearch further into Gods How farre te ſecret and vnſearchable counſels of the vocation of the Gentils & reiecting the deale andto Iewes, otherwiſe then this : that al which be reiected, for their ſinnes be iuſtly reiected, know, in the & al that be ſaued, by Gods great mercie and Chriſt s grace be ſaued. And whoſoeuer doſtriue of ſeeketh among the people to ſpread contagion of curioſity by ſecking furthor after predeſtinatios things paſt mans & Angel s reach, they ouerreach and ouerthrowthenſelues. If thou wilt the ſaued, belecue, obey the Church, feare God and keep his commandements: that is thy part and euery mans els. Thou maiſt not examine whether thou be predeſti- nate or reprobate, nor ſecke to know the waies of Gods ſecret iudgement toward thy ſelf or other men. It is the commou enemy of our ſoules, that in this vnhappy tinie hath The Heretikes opened blaſphemous tongues, and directed the proud pennes of Caluin, Bera, Verone, writings of and ſuch reprobates, to the diſcuſsing of ſuch particulars, to the perdition of many a predeſtination ſimple man, and ſpecially of yong Scholers in Vniuerſities, whichwith leſſe ſtudie may learne to be prowd and cur ious, then to be humble,wiſe, and obedienr.
